structured.approach: Attempts 1 and 2 were refused under G2 for citing file:ap_aging/src/ap_aging/aging.py and file:ap_aging/src/ap_aging/__init__.py. Reading both files again with Read in attempt 2 did not satisfy the checker, and context_list shows they are not context items in this step's contract, so the checker has no receipt for them. For attempt 3 I removed every file: citation. Each repository fact now cites a source the step actually received: the tool view (tool:repo-access) or feat.design, which records the current ap_aging code and version in A3 and B3. I also dropped the cross-check row built on my own Glob/Grep, because that citation was not really tool:repo-access. The output file had picked up repeated '[Tool result]' lines appended outside my writes. I did not carry them into the full rewrite, so they do not pile up. The conclusion has not changed: no database change is needed.

claims.text: The design lists storage, database and schema migration as out of scope. The in-scope data (paid_date key, reject reason, delay history, risk map, overdue rows, CT-1 JSON) is held in memory.
DD-1 says the feature adds no new repository, service, runtime, library or storage. It uses only the Python 3.9 standard library and Node.js 22 CommonJS.

Under NF-10 every new function is pure and in memory: no I/O, no network and no changes to its inputs. A storage or network call from the libraries would reopen DES-01, and this design triggers none of the reopen conditions.

There is no service or transport layer between ap_aging and ap_portal. aging_buckets returns Python values, and aging_buckets, days_past_due, bucket_for and BUCKETS stay unchanged. The ap_aging package version is 1.4.0 today.
The Backend tasks TSK-05 (overdue_with_risk) and TSK-06 (overdue_rows_to_json) only change src/ap_aging/aging.py, src/ap_aging/__init__.py and tests/test_overdue.py. TSK-06 adds no transport layer.
ap_aging has no database. No migrations exist and none are needed.

open_questions: Non-blocking, carried over: DQ-1 (feat.design D3) asks which production component carries CT-1 from ap_aging to ap_portal. If the answer adds storage or a transport, DES-01 would reopen and this step would run again.
structured.summary: No database changes are needed for FEAT-ZD-48600 in ap_aging. feat.design rules out storage and migrations (A1, DD-1, NF-10, A8), TSK-05 and TSK-06 only add pure in-memory functions, and the tool view confirms the repository has no database and no migrations. For attempt 3 I removed the source-file citations the checker could not resolve. Every claim now cites feat.tasks, feat.design, tool:repo-access or record:brief. task.db_changes has been rewritten in full with no blocking questions, and BE-04 can start.
